summary: A scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, Beiyin Deng earned a BA from Fudan University, an MA from New York University, and a PhD from Arizona State University. Deng taught at Grinnell College and became Assistant Professor at the University of Missouri in 2024.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Bela Bhattacharya was Professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and later a Professor at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Beligalle Dhammajoti, a scholar in Buddhist studies, earned a PhD from Banaras Hindu University. He has served as Professor at the University of Ruhuna and as Venerable Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Bemé Shyi Drol studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who earned a PhD at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein by 2001. By 2008, he was Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

Ben Williams is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He has held positions at Naropa University and served as the Singhmar Chair in Classical Indian Society and Polity at the University of Alberta (attested 2016).

A scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Lomi earned her PhD from SOAS. She held posts at the University of Virginia, UC Berkeley, and the University of Bristol, where she became Senior Lecturer in East Asian Religions in 2023.
Benhua Yang works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Yang earned a doctoral degree from Nanjing University (2018–2021) and held a post at Anhui University.

Benigno Ferrario was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale." From around 1928 to 1956, he served as Profesor de Lenguas Clásicas y Filosofia at the University of the Republic.

Barua was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned degrees from Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of London (D.Litt.). He served as headmaster at Mahamuni Anglo-Pali Institution and as Professor at the University of Calcutta (1918–1948).

A historian and sinologist, Elman earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held professorships at UCLA and Princeton University, where he directed the East Asian Studies Program in 2002.

Benjamin Bogin, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. (attested 2006). He also studied with Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and Lopon Ugyen Rinpoche.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan from around 2011 to 2017.

Benjamin C. Ray is a religious studies scholar affiliated with the University of Virginia, where he served as Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in the Department of Religious Studies (attested 2000, 2026).

Benjamin Fleming, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, received his PhD from McMaster University. He was a Visiting Scholar at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2010) and held a post at the City University of New York (attested 2021).

A scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Bergmann studied at the universities of Leipzig and Jena before completing his PhD at the University of Tartu (ca. 1814–1816).
Benjamin Goldstein works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. As of 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, supervised by Shayne Clarke.

Babington was an Indologist and linguist who studied at East India Company College and Cambridge (MD). He founded the Madras Literary Society, served as honorary secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society, and worked as a physician at Guy's Hospital.
Benjamin H. Rice was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Homerton College (1834–1836). In 1836, he began serving as a teacher and missionary for the London Missionary Society.
